message_source_quote: Added at layer 20, this answers the FDR-paper "frequency prior" diagnosis for J-lens crowding with an activation-addition-style elicitation direction rather than a mean.
writeup_source_quote: The diagnosis is the frequency-prior account of J-lens crowding: at the read position the uncentred readout `J_l h` is dominated by input-independent continuation tokens ("At", "The", "But", …, whose scores track unigram frequency), and the target sits behind them (or is washed out entirely at the late read layers 26/28/30). The project's existing remedy is to centre the readout, `J_l (h − mu)` — out of scope here, since the readout must stay plain and the vector must be a *direction from a contrast*, not a mean.

differences.what: The message names a specific paper ('FDR-paper') as the source of the frequency-prior diagnosis motivating the method; the write-up states the same diagnosis anonymously, as a given fact about J-lens crowding, without attributing it to any named paper.
differences.message_quote: Added at layer 20, this answers the FDR-paper "frequency prior" diagnosis for J-lens crowding with an activation-addition-style elicitation direction rather than a mean.
differences.writeup_quote: The diagnosis is the frequency-prior account of J-lens crowding: at the read position the uncentred readout `J_l h` is dominated by input-independent continuation tokens ("At", "The", "But", …, whose scores track unigram frequency), and the target sits behind them (or is washed out entirely at the late read layers 26/28/30).

differences.what: Both documents note the existing centring remedy ('J_l(h-mu)') is excluded, but the write-up frames the exclusion as the write-up author's own methodological choice relative to 'the project's existing remedy' (an indirect pointer to the prior method/source in the repo), while the message attributes the exclusion to external 'ground rules', obscuring that this is the repository's own existing prior alternative.
differences.message_quote: Instead of centring the readout (`J_l(h−mu)`, which the ground rules exclude), I steer the **forward pass** toward a state where the model is poised to emit one content word.
differences.writeup_quote: The project's existing remedy is to centre the readout, `J_l (h − mu)` — out of scope here, since the readout must stay plain and the vector must be a *direction from a contrast*, not a mean.

rationale: Neither document explicitly names the white-bear steering source (Raman 2026 or the white-bear-4b note) by name; both only gesture at it indirectly via 'the diagnosis'/'the project's existing remedy' (centring the readout), the prior method being built on/departed from. The message goes slightly further by attaching a label ('FDR-paper') to the diagnosis that the write-up leaves unattributed, giving marginally more source-identifying information, while simultaneously attributing the exclusion of centring to generic 'ground rules' rather than to it being the project's own existing prior remedy as the write-up does; the novelty claim itself (a contrastive elicitation direction built from the benchmark's own read recipes, transferred across families, with zero target leakage) is stated consistently in both documents.
